newsitem.title: SOMALIA: Conflicting reports on Ethiopia-Somalia fight.
newsitem.headline: Conflicting reports on Ethiopia-Somalia fight.

text.p: Moslem fundamentalists in Somalia claimed on Saturday they were pushing back invading Ethiopian forces but other sources said the Ethiopians were advancing.

Ahmed Bile Hassan, a spokesman in Mogadishu for al-Ittihad al-Islami (Islamic Union), said fighters with his group was regaining ground lost in the past three days around the border town of Dolow in southwest Somalia.
But sources from the region said the Ethiopians were pushing deeper into Somalia towards Luq, a major Islamic centre and a base for Moslem Ethiopian rebels according to Addis Ababa.
Independent sources have yet to confirm details of the fighting and Ethiopia has made no official comment.

On Friday Hassan accused Ethiopian troops backed by tanks of pushing 20 km (12 miles) into Somalia and setting up a base in Dhusay village while hundreds of people were fleeing nearby towns held by al-Ittihad.
Dolow, 500 km (300 miles) southwest of Mogadishu, was one of three towns seized by Ethiopian troops in a two-day incursion into western Somalia in August.
Unofficial reports reaching Mogadishu on Saturday said Bula Hawo, a Somali town close to the frontier with Ethiopia and Kenya, was also under threat from Ethiopian forces.
The reports said the town's residents were fleeing.
Hassan gave no casualty figures on Saturday. He said on Friday two Islamic fighters had been killed.
